slots.practicalActivity: Open a new public GitHub repository for Project 1, write a one-paragraph project brief in the README stating what the pool will do and what 'done' looks like, and write one sentence declaring which target role (protocol engineer, full-stack Web3 developer, or security/governance) you're aiming this portfolio at.
slots.deliverable: A new public GitHub repo with an initial README stating your Project 1 brief and your declared target-role emphasis.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: write out, in a planning document, the five 'complete project' criteria this course holds every capstone to — commented contracts with stated simplifications, unit+fuzz+invariant tests, a frontend that reads live on-chain state, a verified testnet deployment, and a tradeoffs-documented README — so you have a concrete checklist to measure all three upcoming projects against.
slots.deliverable: A personal 'definition of done' checklist applied in advance to all three upcoming capstone projects.

slots.practicalActivity: Set up the real project repo layout (contracts/, ignition/modules/, test/, frontend/, hardhat.config.ts), run `npx hardhat init` inside the contracts folder choosing the TypeScript project type, and commit the skeleton with the out-of-scope list (factory, router, fee-switch, flash loans, audit) written into the README.
slots.deliverable: A committed Project 1 skeleton with contracts/test/frontend cleanly separated and an explicit out-of-scope list in the README.

slots.practicalActivity: Write the real `SimplePool.sol` contract (state, `addLiquidity`, `swapAforB`/`swapBforA` with checks-effects-interactions ordering, `removeLiquidity`) plus a `TeachingToken.sol` ERC-20 with a public mint function, and confirm the whole thing compiles with `npx hardhat compile`.
slots.deliverable: A compiling `SimplePool.sol` and `TeachingToken.sol` committed in your project's contracts folder.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: deploy your `SimplePool` and two `TeachingToken`s to a local Hardhat node, mint yourself both tokens, call `addLiquidity` as the very first depositor, and confirm your minted LP shares match the `sqrt(amtA * amtB)` formula by hand-calculating the expected value first.
slots.deliverable: A local deployment of SimplePool with a verified first-deposit share calculation matching the contract's actual output.

slots.practicalActivity: Scaffold the `frontend/` React app with wagmi and viem installed, wire up `usePoolReserves` (reading live reserveA/reserveB) and `useSwap`, and build the two-step approve-then-swap flow end to end against your local Hardhat node and a test wallet.
slots.deliverable: A working React frontend that reads live pool reserves and executes a real approve-then-swap transaction against your local SimplePool.

slots.practicalActivity: Add `testFuzz_Swap` (asserting the constant-product k never decreases) and `invariant_BalanceMatchesReserves` (via `targetContract`) to your test suite, run `forge test`, and write the six-item security-review checklist (reentrancy, overflow, first-depositor, access control, slippage, rounding) into your README with your own findings for each line.
slots.deliverable: A passing fuzz + invariant test suite plus a completed six-item security-review checklist in your README.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: add the `Swap` and `LiquidityAdded` events to `SimplePool`, emit them from every state-changing function, and write a quick script that listens for and logs one real emitted event from a local transaction — your own first taste of the indexing problem Project 2 tackles in depth.
slots.deliverable: An updated SimplePool emitting real events, plus a script confirming one event is captured off-chain.

slots.practicalActivity: Fund a dedicated testnet-only wallet with Sepolia ETH, configure `hardhat.config.ts`'s sepolia network using `configVariable` and `hardhat keystore set` for your RPC URL and private key, deploy via your Ignition module, and verify both tokens and the pool with `npx hardhat verify`.
slots.deliverable: A deployed and verified SimplePool plus two TeachingTokens on Sepolia, with real block-explorer links.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: write Project 1's complete README exactly to the lesson's structure (what it is, architecture summary, out-of-scope list, test coverage, security-review findings, verified Sepolia addresses, frontend link/run instructions), then record a 2-3 minute demo video walking through a live swap against your deployed contract.
slots.deliverable: A finished Project 1 portfolio README plus a recorded demo video of a real swap on your deployed pool.

slots.practicalActivity: Set up Project 2's skeleton (a Hardhat/Foundry contracts folder, a subgraph folder, and a Vite/Next.js frontend folder) and write a one-paragraph README stating this project's scope: one ERC-721 collection, fixed-price approval-based listings, ETH payment, and ERC-2981 royalty payout, explicitly excluding auctions, bundles, ERC-1155, and lazy minting.
slots.deliverable: A committed Project 2 skeleton with an explicit in-scope/out-of-scope README.

slots.practicalActivity: Write the real `SimpleNFTMarketplace.sol` contract (`listItem`, `cancelListing`, `buyItem` with checks-effects-interactions and an ERC-2981 royalty lookup via `_royaltyFor`), deploy a minimal ERC-721 + ERC-2981 test collection, and run through list then buy from a second test account, confirming royalty and seller balances both moved correctly.
slots.deliverable: A deployed SimpleNFTMarketplace plus a test collection, with one real local list-then-buy transaction confirmed via balance checks.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: write a test that lists an NFT and attempts to buy it with the wrong `msg.value`, confirming it reverts, then write a second test confirming `cancelListing` actually removes the listing so a subsequent buy attempt also reverts.
slots.deliverable: Two passing tests proving your marketplace correctly rejects a wrong-price buy and a cancelled listing's buy attempt.

slots.practicalActivity: Build either a subgraph (manifest + `Listing`/`Sale` schema entities + AssemblyScript `handleListed`/`handleSale` mappings) or a custom ethers.js event listener against your deployed marketplace, and confirm a real test listing and sale both show up correctly in a query within a few blocks, including the `active` flag flipping to false on sale.
slots.deliverable: A working indexer (subgraph or custom listener) correctly reflecting one real listing and one real sale from your deployed contract.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the connect-wallet, list-NFT (two-transaction approve-then-list), and buy-NFT flow in React with ethers v6's `BrowserProvider`, feeding the listings grid from your indexer, and handle the unhappy path where `buyItem` reverts because someone else already bought it.
slots.deliverable: A working frontend that lists and buys a test NFT end to end against your own testnet deployment, including a handled revert case.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: run your full marketplace demo end to end on a testnet — connect two separate test wallets, list an NFT from one, buy it from the other, and confirm the indexer's active flag and your frontend's listings grid both update correctly afterward.
slots.deliverable: A completed, verified end-to-end testnet demo (list + buy across two real wallets) with indexer state confirmed correct.

slots.practicalActivity: Write Project 2's finished README using the four-part structure (problem/architecture, tech stack and tradeoffs, how to run it, known limitations), record a 2-3 minute demo video, and write your own answers to the three standard interview questions (why approval over escrow, why an indexer, how you handled royalties) in your own words.
slots.deliverable: A finished Project 2 portfolio README, a demo video, and written answers to three interview questions about your own design choices.

slots.practicalActivity: Before writing any code, sketch the four contracts this project needs (governance token, Governor, TimelockController, proposal UI) in a planning document with one sentence on what each is responsible for.
slots.deliverable: A written four-contract architecture sketch for your DAO governance system.

slots.practicalActivity: Write the real `GovernanceToken` contract (ERC20 + ERC20Permit + ERC20Votes with the required `_update` and `nonces` overrides), deploy it to a local network, mint yourself a balance, call `delegate()` on your own address, and confirm `getVotes()` returns your balance, not zero.
slots.deliverable: A deployed GovernanceToken with confirmed, working self-delegation and nonzero voting power.

slots.practicalActivity: Deploy a `TreasuryTimelock` (`TimelockController`) locally with a short test-only `minDelay`, grant `PROPOSER_ROLE` to a placeholder address standing in for your Governor and `EXECUTOR_ROLE` to the zero address, then renounce the deployer's admin role and confirm with `hasRole()` that it's actually gone.
slots.deliverable: A deployed TimelockController with the deployer's admin role confirmed renounced via `hasRole()`.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: write a test that attempts to grant a role on your TimelockController from the deployer account after renouncing admin, and confirm it reverts — proving in code, not just by inspection, that the backdoor is actually closed.
slots.deliverable: A passing test proving the renounced deployer can no longer grant timelock roles.

slots.practicalActivity: Write the real `ProjectGovernor` contract (Governor + GovernorCountingSimple + GovernorVotes + GovernorVotesQuorumFraction + GovernorTimelockControl with all six required overrides), deploy all three contracts in the correct order with role grants, submit a test proposal, vote it to success, queue it, wait out the delay, and execute it.
slots.deliverable: A fully wired Governor + token + timelock deployment with one real proposal walked from propose() through execute().

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: build a minimal proposal UI that decodes and displays a proposal's actual `targets`/`values`/`calldatas` — not just its text description — and shows live for/against/abstain tallies and the current `ProposalState` for your deployed Governor.
slots.deliverable: A working proposal UI that decodes and displays the real on-chain calls a proposal will execute, plus its live vote tallies.

slots.practicalActivity: Run the full testing checklist from the lesson against your own deployment (delegation works, every proposal state transition happens correctly, quorum actually gates execution, the timelock delay is real, the deployer's admin role is gone), writing down the actual result of each check, then write two to three sentences naming your design's single point of failure and what you'd change to mitigate it.
slots.deliverable: A completed, evidence-backed testing checklist plus a written single-point-of-failure analysis for your DAO.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: practice and time your full proposal-lifecycle demo (verified contracts, submit, vote, Succeeded, queue with eta, execute) until you can run it live in under three minutes from a cold deployment, then write Project 3's finished README using Projects 1 and 2's same structure (architecture, tradeoffs, how to run it, known limitations, verified addresses).
slots.deliverable: A timed, under-three-minute live demo script plus a finished Project 3 portfolio README with verified contract links.

slots.practicalActivity: Take one deliverable from each of your three capstone projects and write one action+artifact+proof bullet for each (naming the real technique, a real number where honest, and a real verifiable link — Etherscan, GitHub, or a demo URL), then assemble them into a one-page resume using the lesson's six-section structure.
slots.deliverable: A one-page blockchain developer resume with nine real, link-backed action+artifact+proof bullets across your three capstones.

slots.practicalActivity: Pin your three capstone repos on GitHub, rewrite your strongest project's README using the five-part structure (description, architecture, verified address, test command + coverage, key design decisions), and test every link in it to confirm none are dead or unverified.
slots.deliverable: Three pinned GitHub repos plus one rewritten, five-part, link-tested README for your strongest project.

slots.practicalActivity: Write out, from memory and in your own words, the full transaction-lifecycle answer (sign, broadcast, mempool, nonce, inclusion, execution, success/revert), then write one sentence each explaining reentrancy, an access-control gap, and why `tx.origin` is unsafe for authorization, without looking back at the lesson.
slots.deliverable: A written, from-memory set of answers to the transaction-lifecycle and three security-pitfall interview questions.

slots.practicalActivity: Write one more deliberately buggy Solidity function of your own (reentrancy, an unchecked arithmetic risk, or a missing access check) and walk a study partner — or narrate out loud to yourself and record it — through the five-step review method to find it, without revealing the category in advance.
slots.deliverable: One original buggy function plus a recorded or written walkthrough applying the five-step security-review method to find it.

slots.practicalActivity: Using at least two source types (an aggregated salary site and a set of live job postings under at least two blockchain-role title variants), research a realistic low-to-high compensation range — base and any token component — for your target experience level and company stage, and write down the sources behind each number.
slots.deliverable: A sourced, low-to-high compensation range for your target blockchain engineering role, with named sources.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student has three complete, portfolio-ready flagship projects — a tested and verified DeFi liquidity pool, an indexed NFT marketplace with a wallet-connected frontend, and a timelock-governed DAO with a working proposal lifecycle — plus a resume, GitHub presentation, and rehearsed interview answers; this closes out the entire Blockchain Engineer path with a demonstrable, end-to-end track record ready to show an employer.
